subject.title: fix(infra): fix exec-approvals async lock, not just the sync path (#106777, extends #108971)

question: Should OpenClaw retain exec-approvals' lock implementation locally to enforce its authorization-specific nonce and reentrancy contract, or should the equivalent ownership fix be made in the shared fs-safe dependency and consumed through its public lock API?
rationale: Both paths affect the fail-closed authorization boundary and ownership semantics for other callers; source-level test coverage alone cannot decide the intended dependency and security-owner boundary.

options.title: Adopt one local owner-scoped fix
options.body: Choose one rebased PR, prove current-head Docker/VirtioFS cleanup and contention behavior, and retain the local contract only for exec-approvals.

options.title: Fix the shared lock package first
options.body: Move the filesystem-identity correction into the shared dependency if maintainers want one lock contract for all consumers, then keep exec-approvals focused on its policy-specific fail-closed handling.

options.title: Pause both parallel PRs
options.body: Defer landing until the desired ownership boundary and proof requirements are agreed, avoiding two competing implementations of a security-sensitive lock.

recommendation.title: Adopt one local owner-scoped fix
recommendation.body: Choose one rebased PR, prove current-head Docker/VirtioFS cleanup and contention behavior, and retain the local contract only for exec-approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: The related nonce-based lock design is the direct predecessor of the ownership model under review.
